result.evidence:
THE CLAIM UNDER TEST, SPLIT IN TWO

(a) "no anti-oscillation term in _move_toward" — TRUE, and provable by direct comparison inside the same file. The transit tie-breaks are `(dist_after, preferred)` (agents.py:1152) and `(risk, dist_after, preferred)` (1160-1164). The retreat path, forty lines earlier, does have one: `if ncell == last_cell: continue` (883-884), fed by `_idle_retreat_last_cell` (854, 994), and the code calls it "the anti-oscillation memory" in its own comments (904-905, 998). _move_toward neither reads nor writes that attribute.

(b) "there is no mechanism to repair" — FALSE. Five exist outside _move_toward.

WHY A STABLE 2-CYCLE NEEDS BOTH CELLS CLEAN

The measured signature is _move_toward <-> _move_toward, i.e. the survival gate did not fire at either end. By agents.py:688-700 that means A and B are each not-burning, not-smoky and not 4-adjacent to fire. Tier 3 (1143-1146) only ever hands back a cell that is `not adjacent_fire and not smoke`, so B is clean by construction too. At A, tiers 1 and 2 are empty, so every improving and every maintaining neighbour of A is excluded at 1137/1141 — and it cannot be excluded by being fire itself (1107), because a burning 4-neighbour of A would make A adjacent to fire and route it through _survival_move. So every blocked neighbour is blocked by adjacent_fire or by smoke. That yields a clean dichotomy, and both halves have a bounded clock:

  Flavour 1 (adjacency): some burning F is 4-adjacent to a neighbour of A, so |F-A| <= 2; A not adjacent to fire forces |F-A| == 2 exactly. _needs_immediate_survival_retreat fires at distance 1. The dither therefore lives in a one-cell-wide band, one step of fire spread away from being taken over by _survival_move — which does have the anti-oscillation memory.

  Flavour 2 (smoke): the blocking neighbours are smoky but not adjacent to fire, which happens behind the front on recently-burnt ground. Neither the survival gate nor route_blocked can see it. The repair is smoke expiry, and for a burnt cell that runs once per TICK (agents.py:91-94 short-circuits before the %3 gate), decrementing a counter that started at the cell's initial fuel (7..10).

THE BOARD IS NOT FROZEN, AND EVERY HAZARD IS ONE-SHOT

`burning` can only change on ticks divisible by FIRE_SPREAD_SPEED=3 (agents.py:97 and 121), and because every Fire agent is built in reset() before the first step (wildfire_model.py:129 -> 1968-1995; line 1989 is the only agents.Fire( call in the file), all Fire agents share one steps_counter, so the whole board flips together on 1-in-3 ticks. Fire agents are inserted into the OrderedDict-backed scheduler before Firefighter markers, and mesa 1.2.1's SimultaneousActivation iterates insertion order twice (.venv/Lib/site-packages/mesa/time.py:138-151), so Fire.advance runs before Firefighter.advance within a tick — the firefighter sees the post-flip board on the same tick.

The decisive structural fact is that both hazard states are absorbing-to-clean per cell:
  - burnt: set at agents.py:109-112, and then 91-92 forces next_burning_state False and 122-124 forces burning False forever. A cell burns at most once.
  - smoke: activation at 158-167 requires `dispelling_counter == dispelling_counter_start_value`, which is false forever after the first decrement at 173; and once 177 sets smoke=False the `elif self.smoke` branch is dead. A cell smokes at most once.
With DENSITY_PROB = 1 every cell carries fuel and a Smoke object, so this applies everywhere. Arithmetic over BURNING_RATE=1, FIRE_SPREAD_SPEED=3, fuel in [7,10], SMOKE_PRE_DISPELLING_COUNTER=2 gives per-cell hazard windows of roughly T..T+25 (fuel 7) to T..T+34 (fuel 10) ticks from ignition. The hazard configuration that creates any particular 2-cycle is therefore guaranteed to dissolve, on a deterministic clock. That is the repair mechanism the brief says does not exist, and it is the only one that fires unconditionally.

WHAT route_blocked ACTUALLY DOES — AND WHY IT USUALLY CANNOT REACH THIS

It is not a log-only path. agents.py:1070-1072 calls the model handler inline; wildfire_model.py:4033-4066 records the event and enqueues; 2881-2912 issues a physical `unassign` — which clears assigned, target_pos, rescued_victim, exiting (3592-3596) — and then runs select_rescue_assignment to hand the victim to a different unit. All of it executes synchronously at agents.py:1130, BEFORE the dithering unit's own grid.move_agent at 1176. So the unit takes one more step and then has no target at all. That decisively ends a dither, within the same tick.

Two things gate it hard. First, `route_blocked_now` is `not _path_exists_avoiding_fire(...)` (1099-1103), and that BFS excludes only active fire (`if cell in fire_cells: continue`, 1061) — smoke and adjacency are invisible to it. So for both dither flavours above, if any fire-free corridor to the target exists, route_blocked_now is False by construction and this path never runs. Second, even when it does run, `_blocked_replacement_attempted` (wildfire_model.py:2888-2891) allows it once per (firefighter, victim) pair for the whole run, and grep shows that set is written only at __init__ (282) and 2891 — never cleared.

For an exiting unit it is disabled outright: agents.py:1100 `if not self.exiting:` guards the entire computation, and 685 disables _needs_immediate_survival_retreat for exiting units as well. A carrying unit that dithers has no hazard response of any kind beyond _move_toward's own tiers.

THE ONE GLOBAL NO-PROGRESS TIMEOUT IS DEFEATED BY THE DITHER'S OWN SIGNATURE

_update_unreachable_victims runs unconditionally every step (wildfire_model.py:4638) with UNREACHABLE_STREAK_STEPS=30. It computes `approaching` as `dist < prev` against last step's distance (3940-3943); rescue_planner.py:443-448 treats that as "productively served"; 499-502 resets the streak to 0 whenever served OR geo_reachable. An A<->B 2-cycle produces distances d, d+1, d, d+1, so `dist < prev` is true on every other step. The streak can never exceed 1. The escape hatch that exists precisely to catch "this rescue is going nowhere" is blind to a 2-cycle because it asks about one step rather than a window.

NO PER-UNIT STUCK DETECTION EXISTS

grep for stuck|oscillat|dither|patience|no_progress across wildfire_model.py returns only _uav_stuck_counts (268, 2370-2392), and _update_uav_stuck_counts_after_move filters to UAV agents. Firefighters have nothing. The only cap is BATCH_SIZE=300 with sys.exit(0) (4600-4605) — that terminates the run, not the dither.

NOTHING WILL TAKE THE TARGET AWAY FROM A HEALTHY UNIT

The assign branch refuses a firefighter already committed to a different victim (3484-3489); _try_dispatch_unresolved_confirmed_victims skips victims that already have an active firefighter (2137-2138); _unassign_firefighter (3779) has no callers anywhere in the repo. target_pos is written at assign (3499) and cleared at unassign (3593) / recycle (2103) and nowhere else — it is never refreshed to the victim's live cell, and Victim.advance is `pass` (agents.py:371-372), so the target is a fixed point. Every unassign site (2830, 2895, 3788, 3990, 4204) is conditioned on victim death, route_blocked, unreachable-escape, or casualty.

THE HONEST STATEMENT, AND THE COUNT

"No repair mechanism inside _move_toward, but five outside it." Ranked by how fast and how reliably each acts on a stable tier3->tier1 2-cycle:

  1. Hazard-field evolution — agents.py:89-125 (fire) and 156-177 (smoke). Unconditional; not a response to the dither at all. Fire flips on 1-in-3 ticks; burnt-cell smoke on every tick. GUARANTEED to break the cycle eventually because each blocking hazard is one-shot with a ~25-34 tick lifetime. This is the answer to the brief's claim.
  2. _needs_immediate_survival_retreat -> _survival_move — agents.py:684-701, 754-863. Breaks flavour 1 after one cell of fire spread (min_fire_distance(A) is provably exactly 2). Disabled for exiting units. Caveat: if _survival_move fails to move the unit, advance falls straight back into _move_toward (468-473), so it is not an unconditional out.
  3. Target loss by victim death — wildfire_model.py:4085-4177 -> 2816-2837. One step after fire reaches the victim's cell.
  4. Firefighter death — wildfire_model.py:4179-4252. Same step the fire arrives.
  5. route_blocked replacement — agents.py:1130 -> wildfire_model.py:4033-4066 -> 2881-2912. Instant and decisive when it fires, but only for the fire-topology flavour, only once per (ff, victim) pair, and never for an exiting unit.

Provably inert against this signature, and therefore not part of the count: _update_unreachable_victims (defeated by alternating `dist < prev`), any form of preemption (does not exist), any firefighter stuck counter (does not exist).
result.uncertainties:
Not measured, only reasoned from source — I did not run the simulation, per the brief.

1. How often the hazard mask actually changes in a dithering unit's 5-cell neighbourhood. I proved the mechanisms exist and their clocks (1-in-3 ticks for fire, per-tick for burnt-cell smoke) but not the empirical rate. The claim "the board changes every step in practice" is INFERRED, not proved.

2. The split between the two dither flavours. I proved the dichotomy is exhaustive (adjacency-blocked vs smoke-blocked) but not which dominates the 144 observed reversals. That split matters: flavour 1 is broken by survival retreat within roughly one spread event, flavour 2 only by smoke expiry. Classifying the 144 by whether min_fire_distance(A) == 2 at the reversal would settle it and is cheap to add to the existing instrumentation.

3. Mean dither duration. My argument bounds the LIFETIME of any single blocking hazard (~25-34 ticks per cell) but not the duration of a dither, because the front can ignite fresh cells next to A while old ones burn out. Whether observed reversals are 2-4 steps long or 30+ is exactly the measurement that decides DEFECT vs MEASUREMENT, and I do not have it. The prior reports counted reversals, not run-lengths.

4. Tick-alignment of the smoke arithmetic. My T+9 / T+30 / T+34 figures assume ignition lands on a multiple of FIRE_SPREAD_SPEED, which it does (advance only flips burning on those ticks), and that the step-before-advance ordering within a tick works as I traced. The ordering is proved; a one-tick offset in the smoke numbers would not change any conclusion.

5. Second-order effect I noticed but did not chase: _move_toward never writes _idle_retreat_last_cell, so a unit alternating between transit and retreat carries a stale anti-oscillation memory into _survival_move. That could weaken repair mechanism 2 in exactly the situation where it is needed. Out of scope for this question; worth a separate look.

6. I did not verify that the route_blocked unassign leaves ff_marker.status untouched has no further consequence — it does (3592-3651 never writes status), which means the unit stays flagged route_blocked and undispatchable until _revalidate_route_blocked_firefighters (2141-2218) clears it. result.new_findings:
COMPLETENESS GAPS - things not looked at that change the framing, though none overturns the memorylessness headline.

1. A GIT REVISION NOT SEARCHED, and it is the load-bearing one. The phrase both prior reports present as their own finding originates verbatim in this branch's own commit c4d5a25 ("last_cell guard: allow the last exit off a burning cell - ff_deaths 16 -> 14 on 23 runs"): "27 of its 30 tight reversals are `_move_toward`-to-`_move_toward` on a path with no anti-oscillation term that this round does not touch". So this round is not independently re-verifying a claim - it is re-verifying a sentence from a commit message that already measured it. Worse for the "neutral absence" framing, the same commit records, from measurement at the call site: "The four unassign-inflow cases are at cur_dist == 1, and `_move_toward` already moves each onto the refused cell in the same step." That is the advance:473 handoff observed live: `_retreat_candidates` refuses a cell via the 883-884 guard, `_survival_move` consequently fails to move, advance:471-473 then calls `_move_toward`, and it steps onto the refused cell in the SAME step. The absence of a guard in `_move_toward` is therefore not merely an absence - the repo's own measured history records it as an override of a guard that is present one call earlier in the same step. That is the single most decision-relevant fact for DEFECT-vs-measurement and the analysis does not contain it. The same commit also reports that the ungated variant reaching those four cases was built and run and is WORSE (tight reversals 5 -> 21, 2 rescues lost) - direct prior evidence on the "would adding a damper help" question, uncollected.

2. A REGIME NOT NAMED. `_needs_immediate_survival_retreat` (685-686) and `_idle_needs_survival_move` (704-705) both return False when `self.exiting` is True. So for a unit carrying a victim, `_move_toward` (advance:557) is the ONLY mover in every hazard condition - the entire guarded retreat path is unreachable. The analysis notes `exiting` gates the BFS at 1100 but never notes it disables every guarded mover. result.new_findings:
TIER 2 IS UNREACHABLE DEAD CODE -- the structure is 3-tier, not 4-tier. `maintaining` (agents.py:1115, `dist_after == dist_before`) can never be True. On a 4-connected grid a single step changes Manhattan distance by exactly +/-1: for a step (+1,0), dist_after - dist_before = |cx+1-tx| - |cx-tx|, which is +1 when cx >= tx and -1 when cx < tx; never 0. Therefore `tier_pools[1]` (agents.py:1139-1142) is ALWAYS empty and `chosen_tier` can never take the value 2. I confirmed this arithmetically by exhaustive enumeration over a 12x12 grid (76032 neighbour steps, 0 cases with dist_after == dist_before) and closed the only escape hatch -- non-integer targets -- by checking every writer: wildfire_model.py:3499 `victim_cell = (int(victim_pos[0]), int(victim_pos[1]))`, and `exit_target` at agents.py:504-510 built from integer `self.pos` and `H-1`/`W-1`. Consequences: (1) the brief's own 4-tier framing, and any prior round that reasoned about tier-2 behaviour, was reasoning about a pool that never fills; (2) the movement-reason telemetry ("risk tier {self._last_move_tier}", agents.py:479/529) can never emit 2, so tier histograms in earlier probe output should show a hole at 2 -- if any prior run reported tier 2, that measurement is wrong; (3) it slightly simplifies their static-grid reversal construction, which over-specifies by requiring "improve or maintain" neighbours to be dirty.

ROUTE-BLOCKED SIGNAL IS INVARIANT ALONG A CYCLE. Proved from `_path_exists_avoiding_fire` (1030-1065): `src` is never fire-tested (1049) and `dst` is accepted before the fire filter (1059 precedes 1061), so for two adjacent non-fire cells A,B -- guaranteed by 1107 for any `_move_toward` step -- BFS from A and from B return identical results. `route_blocked_now` therefore cannot differ at the two ends of an A<->B oscillation under a frozen grid. Combined with the 1068 de-dup, this makes 1130 a one-shot at episode entry. This is the sharpest available discriminator for the next round and it is stronger than the one the analysis proposed.

`_move_toward` IS ALSO BLIND TO OTHER UNITS, not just to its own past. `_cell_contains_active_fire` (633-638), `_cell_has_active_smoke` (645-656) and hence `_firefighter_cell_risk` (665-673) all filter `type(agent) is Fire` / `type(agent) is not Fire: continue`. Nothing inspects other Firefighters, Victims or PathMarkers occupying a neighbour cell, and mesa's MultiGrid permits co-location. So two units with the same target and the same position make byte-identical choices, and a unit will step onto a cell another unit occupies. If any of the 144 measured reversals involve co-located or adjacent units with a shared target, that is a second, independent structural driver the prior reports did not separate out from the "no anti-oscillation term" story.

THE 1123-1125 EARLY RETURN LEAVES TIER TELEMETRY STALE. When every in-bounds neighbour is burning, `scored` is empty, `_mark_route_blocked()` fires at 1124 and the method returns at 1125 WITHOUT reaching the writes at 1169-1170. The unit does not move, but `advance` then reports `self._last_move_tier` from the previous step at agents.py:479/483, 529/532 and 569. Pure telemetry defect with no control-flow effect (it in fact reconfirms that `_last_move_tier` is not a damper), but it means "risk tier" values in prior probe output are not reliably per-step, and a "holding, surrounded" step is mislabelled with the last successful step's tier.

DEATH IS NOT AN INDEPENDENT CYCLE TERMINATOR. wildfire_model.py:4190 `if cell not in fire_cells: continue` gates `ff_marker.dead = True` (4211) on the unit's own cell burning, which is a grid change by definition. So the one obvious extra terminator I looked for folds into their cause (i). End-of-run does not, and remains uncovered by their binary.

  -> min = (10,6) = A                               ***TIER 4***

  advance() diverts at both (both smoky). At A, _pick_improving_retreat returns None
  (no candidate gains fire distance or lowers risk at equal distance), so
  _survival_move falls to the max-by-(dist,-risk) branch (818-821) and moves to
  (10,5); _idle_retreat_last_cell is then (10,6), which the anti-oscillation filter
  (883) removes from the next scan, and the unit walks off to (11,5). No cycle.

=====================================================================
2. (iii) LONGER LIMIT CYCLES
=====================================================================
ODD LENGTHS -- IMPOSSIBLE. Lemma A gives exactly +/-1 per step; a closed orbit needs
  as many +1 as -1 steps, so its length is even.

LENGTH 4 -- IMPOSSIBLE (all tier combinations). The only 4-step orbit with distinct
  cells in a 4-connected grid is a unit square. Its corner distances are forced:
  moving +/-x changes dist by a sign that is constant across the square (T.x cannot
  lie strictly between two consecutive integers), same for y. So the corners are
  P=a, Q=a+1, S=a+1, R=a+2 with Q and S each adjacent to BOTH P and R.
  Traverse P->Q->R->S->P (the reverse is symmetric):
    Q->R worsens => Q uses tier 3 or tier 4.
    CASE Q tier 3: needs R clean, and needs NO clean improving neighbour at Q. P is
      an improving neighbour of Q and cannot be a fire cell (the unit stands on it),
      so P must be dirty. A dirty P can only be entered by tier 4, so S uses tier 4;
      tier 4 at S means every non-fire neighbour of S is dirty, and R is such a
      neighbour -> R dirty. Contradicts R clean. DEAD.
    CASE Q tier 4: then every non-fire neighbour of Q is dirty, so P and R are dirty,
      so S must also use tier 4 to land on the dirty P. Now compare keys (1160-1163):
        f(Q)=R requires (risk R, a+2, .) < (risk P, a, .)  => risk(R) < risk(P) STRICT
        f(S)=P requires (risk P, a,   .) < (risk R, a+2, .) => risk(P) <= risk(R)
      Direct contradiction. DEAD.
  (P cannot be fire -- it would be dropped at 1107 and never chosen by S. R cannot be
   fire -- same reason at Q.)

LENGTH 6 -- IMPOSSIBLE when no cell uses tier 4. In the tier-4-free case every cycle
  cell is clean (tier1/tier3 picks are clean-only). Take a global-minimum-distance
  cell; its successor is at a+1, so it used tier 3; from that successor the min cell
  is a CLEAN IMPROVING neighbour, so the successor must use tier 1 and returns to
  distance a. By induction the cycle alternates strictly between distance rings a
  and a+1. But any 2x2 block of cells spans THREE distinct distances (p, p+ex, p+ey,
  p+ex+ey with ex,ey in {+1,-1}), and the only length-6 grid cycle is a 2x3 boundary,
  all four cells of whose left 2x2 sub-block are on the cycle. Contradiction.

LENGTH >= 8 -- NOT PROVED IMPOSSIBLE, but heavily constrained. In the tier-4-free
  case the cycle must lie in the two-ring annulus {a, a+1}, which contains no 2x2
  block, so it must wind all the way around the target; and three extra necessary
  conditions fall out of the tie-breaks:
    (a) every tier-1 step must be exactly the greedy `preferred` step -- because at a
        ring-(a+1) cell both its predecessor and successor are clean improving
        neighbours, so if the predecessor is `preferred` the unit turns straight back
        (a 2-cycle);
    (b) no ring-a cell may be entered from its +x neighbour -- if it were, that
        neighbour sits at the head of the (+1,0),(-1,0),(0,+1),(0,-1) order and,
        being clean, is the tier-3 pick, so the unit turns straight back;
    (c) every ring-(a-1) cell adjacent to the loop must be hazardous (a complete
        hazard shell one ring inside the loop).
  The canonical candidate is the 8-cycle around a sealed target. Hand-executed with
  T=(10,10) and the target cell itself dirty:
    at (11,10): improving nbr is only T, dirty -> tier1 empty; tier3 order is
      (12,10), T, (11,11), (11,9); with (12,10) blocked the pick is (11,11).
    at (11,11): dx=-1, dy=-1, abs>=abs -> preferred = (10,11) -> tier1 picks (10,11).
    at (10,11): tier1 empty again; tier3 order is (11,11), (9,11), (10,12), T.
      (11,11) MUST be clean (it was just chosen by tier 3 at (11,10)), and it is
      first in the order -> the pick is (11,11), NOT (9,11).
    => the 8-cycle collapses into the 2-cycle (10,11) <-> (11,11).
  The +x-first ordering systematically collapses loops back into 2-cycles.

=====================================================================
3. DIRECT ANSWERS
=====================================================================
(i)  BOARD PROPERTY. Necessary and sufficient (clean case, the one that runs):
     two adjacent CLEAN cells A, B with dist(B) = dist(A)-1 >= 1 such that
       (1) every neighbour of B strictly closer to the target is fire, fire-adjacent
           or smoky  -- B's entire forward cone is hazard-sealed, with B itself
           outside the seal;
       (2) A is the FIRST clean neighbour of B in the order (+1,0),(-1,0),(0,+1),(0,-1);
       (3) B is A's tier-1 minimum -- B is A's `preferred` cell, or A's preferred cell
           is not clean-improving and B is the first clean improving neighbour of A.
     (1) is the substantive condition; (2) and (3) are tie-break bookkeeping that
     always resolve to something. In one sentence: a hazard curtain laid exactly
     across the forward cone of a clean cell, one step behind which lies a clean
     fallback that itself points back at the curtain. No memory, no history, no
     dynamics are required -- purely a static property of the hazard set.

(ii) NO. _move_toward never evaluates the standing cell's hazard status: the loop at
     1105-1121 iterates only _neighbor_cells() (675-682), and the standing cell
     enters only through dist_before (1092), the `preferred` geometry (1083-1091),
     and _path_exists_avoiding_fire (1101-1103), which feeds only the status signal.
     _firefighter_cell_risk is never called on self.pos. Nor is there a stay-put
     option: line 1176 moves unconditionally, and the only non-moving exit (1123-1125)
     needs every in-bounds neighbour to be burning.
     WHAT FOLLOWS FOR tier3->tier1: the tier-3 retreat is uncosted and unconditional.
     The unit steps to a strictly worse cell purely because that neighbour is clean,
     without ever asking whether the cell it already occupies is at least as good,
     and without the option to hold. Combined with memorylessness (Lemma E) this
     makes the tier3<->tier1 2-cycle the inevitable fixed point of an always-move
     policy whose forward cone is sealed -- not a broken branch. The check that
     _move_toward lacks exists one level up: advance():460 does evaluate the standing
     cell, which is precisely why the reachable cycle is a CLEAN-cell cycle.
     (Two further inert details fall out of the same reading: in tier 1 the
     `dist_after` component of the key at 1152 is always a tie, and in tier 3 the
     `preferred` component is always False -- each tier uses exactly one half of a
     two-part key.)

(iii) The 2-cycle is the worst case in practice. Odd cycles are impossible (parity);
     4-cycles are impossible for every tier combination; 6-cycles are impossible
     whenever tier 4 is not involved; and the canonical 8-cycle collapses into a
     2-cycle under the fixed neighbour ordering. I did not prove L>=8 impossible in
     general, but any such cycle needs a hazard shell fully encircling the target
     plus a tie-break rotation the (+x,-x,+y,-y) order actively fights.

(iv) SAFE. Both cells of a tier3<->tier1 cycle are clean by construction -- B is A's
     tier-1 pick (1137: not adjacent_fire, not smoke; 1107: not fire), A is B's
     tier-3 pick (1145-1146: same). Independently, advance() only reaches line 522
     when the standing cell is fire-free, smoke-free and strictly more than 1 cell
     from any fire (684-701). In Construction 1 the min-fire distances are 3 at A and
     2 at B. The unit is in no danger whatsoever; the loss is mission time, and it is
     invisible -- route_blocked is not raised, because a fire-free route to the victim
     genuinely exists and the unit is simply unwilling to walk the fire-adjacent cell
     on it. A safe, silent, indefinite stall.
